content:
anya (support): Acadia Health escalated — p99 latency for /v1/generate up ~8x since 03:10 UTC in us-west-2. They report user timeouts and session drops. sample req ids: req_abc123, req_def456.
sofia (eng-infra): Noted. Any infra rollouts around that time?
anya (support): They say no changes on their side. p95 ~180ms unchanged, p99 jumped to 3.2s from baseline ~400ms. Model: redwood-large-v2-quant, pool rw-usw2-gpu-v3. Hosts involved: host-uw2-12, host-uw2-15.
matt (eng-runtime): Can you paste host kernel + driver versions and any deploy logs for that pool? Also need per-token breakdown if available.
anya (support): Kernel 6.1.21, nvidia-driver 535.86 (rolled to that pool at ~02:50 UTC). Deploy-bot: "driver-rollout to rw-usw2 completed 02:52 UTC". Attached request traces and headers.
sofia (eng-infra): We rolled 535.86 to rw-usw2 at 02:50. I see nvme tail latency on host-uw2-15 spike at 03:05 correlating with p99. nvme p99 jumped 4ms -> 42ms. dmesg shows nvme timeout/reset entries.
lee (eng-sre): Could be driver/kernel/firmware interaction. Any GPU SM stalls or nvidia-smi indications?
matt (eng-runtime): Runtime traces show long waits in IO before GPU submit. Anonymized trace snippet:
```
req req_abc123: tokenize 12ms -> enqueue 8ms -> nvme_wait 34ms -> gpu_submit wait 1200ms -> complete
```
KV cache miss rate increased ~20% in the window.
sofia (eng-infra): Host dmesg excerpt:
```
[03:06:12] nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 timeout, aborting command
[03:06:12] nvme nvme0: reset controller
```
Note: driver 535 introduced a new NVMe power-management path that touches submission queues.
lee (eng-sre): Short term mitigation ideas: route affected customer to older pool/hosts, or rollback driver on impacted hosts. Can we route Acadia to rw-usw2-gpu-v2 (older stable pool) while we triage?
anya (support): Acadia requires quick fix. Route switch needs to be transparent for them — can we do it safely?
matt (eng-runtime): Yes. We can add a routing rule to prefer rw-usw2-gpu-v2 for customer_id=acadia for 15 minutes while we triage. I'll push the change.
deploy-bot: Routing policy update #785 applied: route(acadia)=rw-usw2-gpu-v2 (TTL 15m) at 03:22 UTC by matt
anya (support): Confirmed p99 dropped to ~420ms after route switch. Acadia reports improved experience. :thumbsup:
sofia (eng-infra): For triage we need to repro on a host with kernel 6.1.21 + driver 535.86 and run sustained KV cache heavy workload. I'll prepare repro harness.
matt (eng-runtime): Repro checklist:
- Spin up host with kernel 6.1.21 + driver 535.86
- Load model redwood-large-v2-quant
- Run 200 concurrent short chats with 512 token context and random prefixes to avoid cache hits
- Monitor nvme tail, dmesg, nvidia-smi
Commands:
```
./repro/load_test --hosts host-uw2-15 --concurrency 200 --context 512 --duration 20m
ssh host-uw2-15 'sudo journalctl -k -f' > host-dmesg.log
```
sofia (eng-infra): Also capture NVMe controller FW versions: `nvme id-ctrl /dev/nvme0` — some FWs behave poorly with new driver PM code.
lee (eng-sre): If repro shows nvme resets under sustained qdepth: mitigation options:
- immediate: raise nvme qdepth scheduling and disable aggressive NVMe power mgmt on that pool
- mid: rollback driver to 525.x on impacted hosts (fast but broader impact)
- long: coordinate vendor FW update with OEM and validate driver+FW combo
I'll open infra ticket.
sofia (eng-infra): Created infra ticket INF-2026-113 with logs, dmesg, and repro steps; assigned to storage-team. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2026-113
matt (eng-runtime): Added runtime safety patch idea: if nvme_queue_latency > 50ms then prefer in-memory hotpool or route to fallback model variant. PR #914 (canary off by default).
anya (support): I'll update Acadia: routing change applied + ETA for permanent fix (after triage). Keeping them in the loop.
lee (eng-sre): Next steps: repro on 535.86 hosts -> determine root cause (driver vs NVMe FW vs kernel interaction). If driver, coordinate rollback + postmortem. If FW, engage vendor for firmware. We keep this thread open until RCA and customer comms are complete.
anya (support): Thanks everyone. Will post updates and escalate if Acadia reports anything else.
